specification.problem: Fixed-point amplitude amplification: given a state preparation A with |psi>=A|0>=sqrt(lambda)|good>+sqrt(1-lambda)|bad>, and only a lower bound lambda_0 <= lambda, boost success probability to at least 1-delta^2 (adjustable failure bound) for all lambda in a range, using O(1/sqrt(lambda_0)) oracle queries (quadratic speedup).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Background-only reconstruction of the standard amplitude amplification setting and the failure-probability criterion, plus a tiny explicit Grover-iterate instance (one step, lambda=1/4). The paper's specific fixed-point construction with quadratic speedup (its phase schedule and range-optimality guarantee) is outside scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: initial overlap fraction (success probability) of target states in the initial state

equations.label: Initial decomposition
equations.description: Initial state split into target and non-target parts with fraction lambda
equations.abstract_quote: what fraction $\lambda$ of the initial state is comprised of the target states
equations.justification: The abstract defines lambda as the target fraction; the amplitude form is the standard interpretation.

equations.label: Standard Grover iterate
equations.latex: G=-A S_0 A^{\dagger} S_g,\quad S_g=I-2|g\rangle\langle g|\text{ (oracle)},\quad S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle 0|
equations.description: Standard amplitude amplification iterate, one oracle query per application
equations.justification: Textbook amplitude amplification; not the paper's fixed-point operator.
assumptions: Oracle marks good states by phase flip

equations.label: Standard amplification success probability
equations.description: Success probability after L Grover iterations; oscillates and overshoots if lambda is unknown
equations.justification: Standard result; illustrates why plain Grover is hard to use without knowing lambda.
assumptions: Exact Grover iterate with pi phases

equations.label: Fixed-point requirement
equations.description: Target property: failure bound satisfied for all lambda above the lower bound, with a quadratic-speedup query count. The log(1/delta) scaling is a typical form, not claimed by the abstract.
equations.abstract_quote: need only a reliable lower bound on this fraction
equations.justification: Abstract states adjustable failure bound and quadratic advantage with a lower bound on lambda; the exact query count and range are not given.
assumptions: Range [lambda_0,1] and query scaling form are assumed, not stated; the abstract claims the broadest possible range for a given query count

equations.label: Tiny instance
equations.description: One standard Grover iteration on an instance with lambda=1/4 gives success probability 1
equations.justification: Smallest illustrative instance for later circuit generation.
assumptions: Chosen purely as an illustrative instance

registers.name: search
registers.role: holds the state A|0>, oracle acts on it

registers.name: oracle_flag
registers.role: possible ancilla for marking, not specified in the abstract

steps.description: Apply the standard iterate G; the paper's fixed-point scheme would replace it with a specific unspecified schedule.
Check the requirement against the failure bound over the lambda range.

specification.measurement: Measure the search register (or oracle flag) in the computational basis and test for a target state.
assumptions: Standard amplitude amplification setting with oracle S_g and preparation A
Tiny instance lambda=1/4 chosen as illustration
The paper's actual fixed-point construction is not reconstructed
